name: Vista Roll
summary: A phone photo gallery where pictures grow out of their thumbnails and pinch, pan and swipe like real
about: A phone photo library with nine hand-drawn landscapes from around Pakistan, from Attabad Lake to the lanterns of Anarkali. Tap one and it grows straight out of its thumbnail into a dark viewer where you can pinch, double-tap or scroll to zoom, drag it around with a fling and a soft edge, and swipe to the next picture. Drag it down and it shrinks and flies back into its square in the grid, and the heart keeps a Favourites list.
how: Tap a photo: it grows out of its square into the viewer. Swipe left and right, use the arrows or tap the strip of small photos to move between them.
Pinch with two fingers, double-tap, scroll the mouse wheel or use the plus and minus buttons to zoom up to 400 percent at the spot you choose.
When zoomed, drag to look around: the photo glides on after you let go and springs back from its edges. A single tap hides the bars.
Tap the heart to favourite a photo (a burst and a badge on the grid), then pick Favourites under the grid to see only those.
Swipe down or press Escape to close: the photo shrinks and flies back into its place. Keyboard: arrows change photo, + and - zoom, 0 resets, F favourites.
